raw_response:
I'm 50 years old, been farming this land for 20 years. Never went to school — I can't read those extension pamphlets, but I know my 7 mu of cotton like I know my own hands. My husband works in the city most of the year, sends some money home, but it's not much. It's mostly me and my daughter. She's in school still, so she helps on weekends and after class. We don't have extra cash lying around, so every yuan I spend on inputs means less for emergencies.

This year I'll plant all 7 mu with cotton, same as always. I thought about trying something else once, but cotton is what I know, and the buyer comes to the village to collect it. I plant around April 20th, when the soil gets warm enough. I saved some seed from last year — good habit, saves money — but I'll buy two bags of improved seed to mix in. The old seeds from my own field grow fine, but mixing in some new ones keeps the plants strong.

For fertilizer, I use what I can afford, not what some expert says. Last year I put down about 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time — that's one big bag. Then when the cotton started flowering in July, I topdressed with about 30 jin of urea per mu because the leaves looked a bit yellow. The plants did okay, got about 250 kg per mu of lint. I'll do the same this year. Maybe 12-13 kg of nitrogen total per mu. I don't know exactly what's in the bags, I just know the green bag is for base and the white bag is urea for topdress.

Water costs money to pump from the well. Cotton doesn't need as much as wheat, but if July is dry, the flowers will drop and I'm finished. I'll irrigate twice — once when flowering starts, that's the critical time, and once in August if there's no rain. If it rains enough, maybe only once. The neighbor down the road irrigates three times, but his son has a factory job and sends him more money. I can't spend like that.

Pests are a headache every year. The bollworm is the worst — if you don't watch it, the whole crop is ruined. I spray insecticide two or three times, starting when I see the first worms. I also put down herbicide before planting so I don't have to weed by hand too much. Weeding by hand takes forever and my back isn't what it used to be.

For tillage, I hire Old Wang's small tractor to plow the field after the spring thaw. Costs me about 40-50 yuan per mu, but it's worth it because doing it by hand would take me a week and I'd miss the planting window. After plowing, I break up the clods and make the rows by hand.

Labor is mostly me and my daughter. During planting and the first picking in September, I hire two women from the next village for a few days each. They charge about 80 yuan per day. I need them because my husband won't be back from the city until October, and I can't plant 7 mu alone or pick the first flush by myself.

I expect about 260 kg of lint per mu this year if the weather is normal. Last year was 250 kg/mu. I hope for a little better, but I don't count on it. Cotton prices have been steady, so if I get 250-260 kg/mu, I'll cover my costs and have a bit left for my daughter's school expenses. That's all I ask for — not getting rich, just getting by.
